beats.trigger: Writing a file changes your folder. Slack changes another system.
beats.got: The first practical safety distinction I've heard: an agent that only writes files is low risk, one that posts to another system is not. It writes the message and I approve before it sends.

beats.trigger: Push back when the first answer restates the problem.
beats.got: The agent names the one obstacle that matters. It tends to give me my own problem back first, so I have to push.

beats.trigger: If an agent starts reading the world, stop it, steer narrower, then say *"continue"*.
beats.got: Several agents fetch material from the wiki, our documents and the internet while I supervise. It admits they wander off, which I appreciate. Four windows is a lot of admin, though.

beats.trigger: You can't yet tell if the answer is right. That is expected. Name the doubt; don't fix it here.
beats.got: The output may sound convincing and be wrong, and the course says so outright. That is rare in this kind of material.

beats.trigger: When do you split, and how?
beats.got: A question, not a claim. Fine.

beats.trigger: A hundred tiny agents cost more to coordinate than they save.
beats.got: One agent per recurring job. It sounds like process design, which I already know.

beats.trigger: If one agent can produce what you need, use one.
beats.got: A vendor-style course telling me not to use more of the product. That's the candour I was waiting for.

beats.trigger: A backward planner and a reframer in the same voice are one agent pretending to be two.
beats.got: Three tests for splitting: different access, different dialect, different stance. I could apply these to a real case.

beats.trigger: More input does not fix a beige answer.
beats.got: More agents doesn't mean more rigour. Agreed, and it's the opposite of the usual hype.

beats.trigger: The synthesizer then commits to one diagnosis and drops what does not serve it.

beats.trigger: Could one prompt produce the same quality of output?

take_homes: Default to one agent. Split only when the pieces need different access, different dialect or different stance. A hundred agents are a bigger problem than one.
The failures happen at the handoffs between agents, where a conflicting number is silently dropped. I should check the seams.

misconception.why: I expected more-agents-is-better hype, same as the last programmes. The module said use one agent by default and said plainly that nothing checks the output is true. That is not how the earlier transformations were sold. I still haven't seen a result I can trust, so I'm not convinced, and wait-and-see is not off the table.

one_line: Better than I expected. It told me when not to use it and what it can't check, which the last three programmes never did. I still haven't seen it produce something I'd trust.
